item.title: Said & Checked, Arkansas, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 2 unsupported, 9 unsettled (Sean Duffy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “Reported as: In a post on the social media platform X, Duffy said contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. had secured two routers from FAA facilities in Texas and Arkansas and was conducting "deep diagnostics" on the equipment.” Unsupported. The FAA names two sites, in Amarillo, Texas and El Dorado, Arkansas, and a new router at El Dorado, and says it and L3Harris are still investigating. Neither the FAA nor L3Harris says two routers were secured or that diagnostics are under way; the only source found for that is the secretary's post.
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “Now, we know who did the install. A good American patriot, we believe, a veteran.” Unsupported. No public record identifying the installer, or describing the installer as a veteran, was found. The search covered the FAA's published Q&A, a CNBC report and web searches on the installer; an Arkansas newspaper article could not be read.
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “So we were forced by the telecom provider to actually update that copper to fiber, and we brought in our routers and did the work.” Unsettled. The FAA's published Q&A says copper wires are "being disconnected due to their obsolescence" in this type of work. It does not say the telecom provider retired the El Dorado line or required the move to fiber there. The Transportation Department's Nov. 14 briefing page could not be read.
